abstract_sentences.text: Speech Large Language Models (SLLMs) enable high-level emotion reasoning, but often produce ungrounded, text-biased judgments without verifiable acoustic evidence.
In contrast, SSL encoders such as WavLM yield strong acoustic representations yet remain opaque discriminative models that offer limited interpretability.

To bridge this gap, we introduce the Agentic Decoding of Emotion via Probing Tools (ADEPT) framework, which reframes emotion recognition as a multi-turn inquiry process rather than a single-pass prediction.

ADEPT transforms an SLLM into an agent that maintains an evolving candidate set and adaptively invokes dedicated semantic and acoustic probing tools within a structured pipeline of candidate generation, evidence collection, and adjudication.
Crucially, ADEPT enables a paradigm shift from consensus learning to ambiguity-driven emotion reasoning.
Since human affect exhibits complexity and co-occurrence of emotions, we leverage minority annotations as informative signals instead of discarding them as noise.
Finally, we integrate Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with the Evidence Trust Gate to explicitly couple tool-usage behaviors with prediction quality and enforce evidence-based reasoning.

Experiments demonstrate that ADEPT improves in most cases the primary emotion accuracy while substantially improving minor emotion characterization, producing explanations grounded in auditable evidence.

claim_closure.claim: Tool-mediated multi-turn evidence acquisition yields auditable reasoning.
claim_closure.method_response: Figure 2 and §4 define tools; Phase 3 permits only retrieved observations.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 3 gives one audit-trail example; no audit/user study or error rate is reported.

claim_closure.claim: GRPO plus Evidence Trust Gate prevents non-informative tool use.
claim_closure.method_response: Eq.1–3 gate evidence/tool rewards by correct-versus-incorrect group evidence scores.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 2 reports w/o Trust Gate performance, not a direct reward-hacking behavior measure.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion does not separately revisit the prevention claim.

claim_closure.claim: ADEPT improves primary fidelity and minor/set recovery on MSP-Podcast.
claim_closure.method_response: Metrics distinguish strict primary, relaxed primary, set recall, and Jaccard.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 1 has favorable point estimates; no seed/interval/test accompanies them.

claim_closure.claim: ADEPT allocates more tool budget to more ambiguous items.
claim_closure.method_response: Phase 2 is defined as a conditional computation loop with soft budget.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 4 directly reports increasing calls across the defined label-cardinality groups.

claim_closure.claim: ADEPT is robust to domain shift.
claim_closure.evidence_response: One IEMOCAP zero-shot table supports Set Recall, while Acc/Jaccard are lower than BLSP-Emo.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion says strong zero-shot performance demonstrates robustness.

claim_closure.claim: The formal gate provides a general theoretical guarantee of grounded, causally traceable decisions.
claim_closure.method_response: The paper gives a reward definition and constraints, not a theorem or proof.
claim_closure.evidence_response: No formal guarantee test or theorem statement appears.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion uses evidence-based reasoning language but no theorem.

final_judgment.single_storyline: ADEPT retains consensus-discarded ambiguity as primary/minor candidate structure, probes semantic and acoustic evidence adaptively, then uses an evidence-closed final adjudication; GRPO gates process rewards by outcome-linked evidence behavior.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The main text keeps label rule, phase/tool architecture, Eq.1–3, main result/ablation/transfer tables, and tool-call scaling. It is sufficient for the thesis and headline trade-offs.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendices hold corpus distributions, co-occurrence prior, semantic/acoustic schemas, hard reward rules, sensitivity, mapping details, and prompts. Full executable reproduction depends on those pages.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 2 gives a readable mechanism map, and Table 1 jointly reports primary fidelity, set recovery, and predicted cardinality so the label-expansion alternative can be inspected.
final_judgment.largest_gap: Trust-gate anti-hacking and auditability claims have architecture, an ablation, and an example, but lack direct behavioral audit, seeds/uncertainty, error taxonomy, or a theorem/proof.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a tool-mediated reasoning claim, put task outcome, process behavior, and a calibration quantity that can challenge a trivial more-tools/more-labels explanation in the same main-body argument.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: Use this when tool calls and observations are genuine, inspectable mediators. Do not manufacture process metrics where the task offers no auditable trajectory or observation boundary.
final_judgment.theory_status: Formal reward design only; no theorem statement or proof.

lexical_rhetoric.scope: p.1–8 core main text, using lexical_analysis.py token and stopword conventions; references excluded.

strong_qualified_claim_coding.rule: Manual coding of 26 authorial main-text claim sentences; strong includes achieves/outperforms/direct evidence, qualified includes in most cases/suggest/trade-off framing.

lexical_rhetoric.segmentation_risks: No lemmatization: emotion/emotions and tool/tools remain separate. Title, page header, captions, and repeated method labels inflate agentic decoding and evidence probing title-like n-grams.
